issue.title: Gate command shebangs break when sys.executable contains a space
issue.description:
On Darwin, when `sys.executable` contains a space (this workspace:
`/Users/bbugyi/Library/Application Support/sase/workspaces/.../.venv/bin/python`),
gate command scripts written as `#!{sys.executable}` cannot be exec'd. The kernel
shebang parser splits on the first space and looks for `/Users/bbugyi/Library/Application`.

Reproduced 2026-09-04 while verifying the empty-name identity-facade fix (HEAD
43fe90018). The local identity/link-follow diff does not touch gate command
generation.

1. `just check` escalated to the full suite and failed
   `tests/ace/tui/test_agent_notification_status_overrides.py::test_telegram_gate_resolution_dismisses_and_finalizes_pending_tale_override`
   with `GateError: cannot start command: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '.../commands/approve'`.
2. Isolated rerun of that node failed the same way (1.16s).
3. The `commands/approve` file exists, is mode 0700, and starts with
   `#!/Users/bbugyi/Library/Application Support/sase/workspaces/.../.venv/bin/python`.
4. Direct exec of that file prints: `bad interpreter: /Users/bbugyi/Library/Application: no such file or directory`.
5. `src/sase/notification_gates/command_runner.py::_exec_target` uses `/proc/self/fd/N`
   on Linux (CI) and the raw script path on macOS, so Linux CI never hits this shebang.

The same `#!{sys.executable}` pattern is also in:
`src/sase/plugins/_required_gate_spec.py`,
`src/sase/xprompt/workflow_hitl_gate.py`,
`src/sase/agent/launch_request_gate.py`,
`src/sase/bead/_snooze_gate_spec.py`,
`src/sase/bead/_flag_gate_spec.py`,
`src/sase/bead/_stale_cleanup_gate_spec.py`,
`src/sase/bead/_task_gate_spec.py`,
`src/sase/user_question_actions.py`.
Gate-conformance mobile cases retained failed tmp_path dirs in the same just check
run and likely share this exec path.

task_type_fields.impact:
Any macOS user whose Python lives under a path with spaces — including the
default SASE workspace layout under `~/Library/Application Support/sase/...` —
cannot execute plan-approval and other gate command scripts. Tests that exercise
`execute_gate_selection` fail deterministically on this host; Linux CI does not
see it because those Python paths have no spaces and Linux uses `/proc/self/fd`.
